title: Reset/next-due dates count from the work date, not the paperwork date
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in with View customers, on the build under test. The Maintenance Reminders feature is on (maintenance_reminders flag).
  2. An asset is enrolled with a mileage-triggered service and you can seed exact dated readings (e.g. unit 'ZZAUTOTEST Truck 12'). Compute the expected values by hand to check the product.
custom_steps:
1. Mark a service complete on Monday (the work date) and confirm the next cycle counts from Monday.
  2. Invoice the work order three weeks later and confirm the next due does not move.
  3. Change the proposed reset date and confirm the next due follows it through the service's interval.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The next due counts from the day the work was done (the Reset date), not the invoice/paperwork date.
  • A truck serviced Monday and invoiced three weeks later counts its next cycle from Monday, and invoicing later changes nothing.
  • The proposed reset date is editable and the next due follows it through the service's own interval and updates as it changes.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-3780 (Maintenance Reminders); story SV-10568 (S18, Complete a service); Chunk 2 MR spec (Confluence 897679389), Part 1 / S18 (Rule 116); read 2 Oct 2026. Source-verified 2 October 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S18-R14: “The proposed date is editable and names the day the work was done. The next due follows from it through the service's own interval and updates as it changes, so a shop invoicing weeks late resets from the work rather than from the paperwork”
  • S18-E8: “A truck serviced on Monday and invoiced three weeks later is marked complete on Monday and counts its next cycle from Monday. The worklist shows nothing due for it in between, and invoicing later changes nothing”

AUTOMATION: HOLD - not yet build-verified on a Maintenance Reminders QA build (feature ships behind the maintenance_reminders flag)
